subject: Service outage: closure notice, root-cause summary, and action ledger
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@fintechcorp.com>; Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service outage: closure notice, root-cause summary, and action ledger

Hi Sonia / Rajiv —

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the incident that impacted Redwood's hosted inference endpoints for your account on 2027-03-31. Attached is a concise customer-facing RCA (fintechcorp-rca-summary-20270402.pdf) and an action ledger listing committed mitigations. Below is a short summary and the immediate next steps we recommend.

Summary (TL;DR)
- What happened: A regression in the autoscaler trigger logic combined with a rare model-weight memory spike caused a small set of GPU workers to OOM, which led to request reroutes and increased tail latency between 13:06 and 13:42 PDT on 2027-03-31.
- Impact: Intermittent 5xx errors and elevated latency for ~36 minutes for requests routed to the affected pool. Customer-visible errors for FinTechCorp were limited to approx. 0.8% of requests during that window.
- Root cause: Two factors combined: (1) an autoscaler change deployed 2027-03-28 that reduced the grace period for worker backoffs, and (2) a specific model quantization variant we rolled out for beta customers produced a transient memory allocation pattern not caught by our preflight tests.

Actions we’ve completed (done)
- Rolled back the autoscaler grace-period config for affected pools — completed 03:58 PDT, 2027-04-01.
- Reverted the quantized model variant for production routes for FinTechCorp — completed 14:05 PDT, 2027-03-31.
- Added a short-circuit fallback that routes to warm standby replicas if a worker reports low memory headroom — deployed 2027-04-01.

Committed next steps (action ledger)
1) Safety net: Add automatic memory headroom monitoring + alerting to prevent silent regression — target complete 2027-04-09. (Owner: Stephanie NG)
2) Improved preflight tests: Add model-quantization memory profile tests to CI — target complete 2027-04-16. (Owner: Markus K)
3) Autoscaler tuning: Rework backoff policy and validate under burst scenarios in staging — target complete 2027-04-12. (Owner: Jonas W)
4) Customer follow-up: Schedule a 30-minute postmortem walkthrough with your platform team if useful — please let us know preferred time windows. (Owner: Marissa C)

Attachments: fintechcorp-rca-summary-20270402.pdf (customer-facing RCA), timeline-events-20270329-20270402.csv (event timestamps), mitigations-action-ledger-20270402.md (detailed owners and ETA).

I’ll also paste the condensed timeline in the next message for quick reference. Please reach out with any questions or if you’d like a walkthrough this week.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@fintechcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@fintechcorp.com>, ops@fintechcorp.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service outage: closure notice, root-cause summary, and action ledger

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary and the documents. A couple of quick questions before we escalate internally:

1) You mention 0.8% of our requests were impacted. Can you confirm that this is across all endpoints or only the /generate route? We need per-route numbers for our incident log.
2) For the fallback to warm standby replicas, is that a global behavior or limited to specific pools? Will that change cost profile or latency for normal traffic?

If possible, can we get the per-route breakdown and a very short explanation of cost impact by EOD PST? We’re lining up our internal notes for a 2pm sync.

Best,
Sonia
Director, Platform Engineering
FinTechCorp

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@fintechcorp.com>; Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service outage: closure notice, root-cause summary, and action ledger

Hi Sonia —

Thanks for the quick read-through and great questions. Short answers up-front, followed by the per-route breakdown pasted from our analytics export.

1) Impact by route: The 0.8% figure is across all FinTechCorp-hosted API keys during the window. Breakdown:
- /generate (text gen): 1.1% of route calls returned 5xx or >2s tail latency spikes
- /chat (structured chat): 0.3%
- /embed (batch embeddings): 0.05%

2) Warm-standby fallback behavior: The fallback is per-pool and is only triggered when a worker in the pool reports low memory headroom below the configured threshold. It routes requests to warm standby replicas in the same region (same instance class). We don’t change instance sizing for normal traffic; the fallback may increase token cost slightly for routed requests due to extra routing hops, but our estimates indicate <0.4% incremental cost for FinTechCorp at your normal QPS. We will include an itemized cost check in the action ledger.

Per-route event counts (13:00–14:00 PDT, 2027-03-31):
- /generate: total 92,400 requests, impacted 1,017 (1.1%)
- /chat: total 28,712 requests, impacted 86 (0.3%)
- /embed: total 4,200 batched requests, impacted 2 (0.05%)

We’ve attached the same CSV for your records. If helpful I can convert this into a short-slide summary for your ops review.

Next steps:
- I’ll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with your team if you confirm availability.
- We’ll update the action ledger to include the small cost delta and send a revised ETA column by Monday.

—
Marissa

3) Marissa: once Stephanie has the estimate, I’ll draft a short customer note proposing credit options for legal / finance review.
